DEL-09-02-RQ-001: Section 9 validation additions MUST include the runtime validation IDs enumerated by PRD Section 12.4 and SPEC Section 19.3.

DEL-09-02-RQ-002: validation for section9.runtime_engine_contract MUST confirm Chirality owns an AgentEnginePort / RuntimeEngineContract boundary separate from SDK APIs, covering accepted turn input, UI events, canonical events, permission decisions, permitted tool exposure, session linkage, interrupt/cancel handling, and terminal outcomes.

DEL-09-02-RQ-003: validation for SDK mapping and event-log IDs MUST preserve the distinction between browser UIEvents and persisted HarnessEvents; SDK messages and transcripts are adapter metadata or secondary state unless imported into HarnessEvent form.

DEL-09-02-RQ-004: validation for session replay MUST confirm newline-delimited append order, unique event IDs, no secret storage, artifact references for large payloads, and tolerance for malformed trailing lines.

DEL-09-02-RQ-005: validation for section9.settingsources_isolation MUST confirm shipped runtime does not load ambient user/global Claude Code settings or local .claude/settings.local.json; default settingSources: [] is required where applicable.

DEL-09-02-RQ-006: validation for permission overlay MUST confirm explicit hard-deny precedence, that prompt text and allowedTools alone are not safety boundaries, and that disallowedTools, mode policy, hooks, canUseTool, and/or dontAsk enforce restrictions.

DEL-09-02-RQ-007: validation for Chirality MCP status/dependency tools MUST use mcp__chirality__* naming and confirm MCP tools pass through the same permission, hook, path, redaction, and event logging policy as SDK built-ins.

DEL-09-02-RQ-008: validation for path and instruction-root hooks MUST confirm active project-root containment, instruction-root write denial, initial symlink-write rejection, and fail-closed behavior for write, shell, domain, and subagent actions.
DEL-09-02-RQ-009: validation for tool result budgets MUST confirm large or sensitive tool results are budgeted, previewed, stored as artifacts, or redacted according to policy.
DEL-09-02-RQ-010: validation for compaction MUST confirm compaction boundaries are persisted when available and replay implications are recorded.

DEL-09-02-RQ-011: validation for subagent governance MUST confirm subagent delegation fails closed unless governance gates pass, child capabilities do not expand parent permissions, and child run records/artifact references are produced when execution is enabled.
DEL-09-02-RQ-012: harness runner updates MUST preserve existing Section 8 validation coverage while adding Section 9 IDs as runtime phases land.
DEL-09-02-RQ-013: the summary schema MUST identify Section 9 validation outcomes distinctly enough to support release readiness review; exact schema fields are TBD.

DEL-09-02-RQ-014: each Section 9 ID MUST carry an explicit status and evidence reference or blocker note; runtime phases that have not landed MUST NOT be reported as passing; natural-language status terms MUST preserve the distinction between pass, fail, pending, skipped, blocked, and gated.

DEL-09-02-RQ-015: the registry or manifest evidence SHOULD include each Section 9 ID, source reference, status metadata, warning/blocker notes, and evidence artifact reference when available; exact path and field names are TBD.

DEL-09-02-RQ-016: Section 9 fixture coverage SHOULD be grouped by runtime surface: engine boundary, SDK mapper/event log/replay, settings isolation, permission overlay, tool/MCP exposure, path/instruction-root hooks, tool-result budget, compaction boundary, and subagent governance; exact fixture file paths remain TBD.
